To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hardware implementation of the face detection algorithm is more efficient in terms of speed and power consumption than the software implementation.
The proposed hardware-software codesignment approach is able to achieve acceleration for the face detection algorithm.
the hardware-software codesigned system is able to achieve a real-time face detection rate with the use of a LEON 3 processor and the use of a hardware accelerator module.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a hardware-software implementation of a face detection algorithm.
the development of a face detection system based upon the Viola-Jones method, implemented on an FPGA board.
the design of a real-time face detection system based in a hardware-software co-design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed hardware acceleration mechanism can be used in embedded systems that require real time face detection.
the face detection embedded system based on LEOPARD and LEON 3 is a good alternative to implement real time face detection systems.
this paper presents the hardware implementation of the face detection system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we implemented a face detection system in an FPGA board using an IP module.
the hardware-software codesigned face detection system is able to process a video stream in real-time.
the face detection algorithm is executed in the FPGA and the face recognition algorithm is executed in an ARM processor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have successfully developed a hardware-software co-design technique for a face detection algorithm, and that the hardware-software co-designed system has been implemented on a Xilinx Spartan-3E FPGA.
the face detection process is accelerated in the hardware by 3.7 times.
the face detection algorithm can be accelerated by 3.2 times with respect to a software implementation.
